title.narrative: Strengthening of HIV and Tuberculosis national systems of prevention, treatment, care and support in Georgia - Georgia (01-Jan-2026-31-Dec-2028)

description.narrative: Georgia, TB/HIV, National Center For Disease Control and Public Health (NCDC)This program has the following goals: To turn the HIV epidemic in the reversal phase through strengthened interventions targeting key affected populations (KAP), and significant improvement in health outcomes for PLHIV.. To decrease the burden of tuberculosis and its impact over the overall social and economic development in Georgia, by ensuring universal access to timely and quality diagnosis and treatment of all forms of TB, thus decrease illness, death and drug resistance. The objectives of this program are: To decrease HIV transmission among KPs through expanding access to HIV prevention services. To improve HIV case detection through expanding and diversifying HIV testing services, including various HIV self-testing modalities. To improve access to PrEP among HIV negative MSMs and other KVPs. To improve health and wellbeing of PLHIV through supporting adherence to and monitoring quality of ART services. To strengthen and scale up TB case finding, especially among target groups such as children, contacts, PLHIV, PUD. To improve treatment outcomes through better quality of care, including patient-centered approaches. To scale up TBI screening and preventive treatment.
